distinct: NEXT ACTION: #32 -- fix the §12 marker regexes, then re-run 'agent-yield agents' and RE-SCORE Part C before quoting '4 of 73 carried all three markers' again. That number is a detector floor, not a briefing rate: five Part E dispatches written to §12 exactly scored 0 of 3. Add the five Part E prompts to tests/test_gate.py as CAPTURED positive cases -- the bug survived because the fixtures agreed with the code, which is the #26 failure one file over. Keep --enforce-brief OFF; #27 Stage 2 now has two independent blocks.

#18 IS CLOSED. Part E retracted §11 lever 1: splitting the same task into three agents cost 385,109 tokens against 249,944 as one agent (two replicates), i.e. +54%, against a pre-registered >=1.5x the other way. Write-up in working-method.md §11.1. Corrected everywhere it was quoted, not only where found: agents.py cap comment + render line, §12 rubric row (b), context-cost.html 'split it' row. What is retracted is 'splitting saves', NOT 'splitting never saves' -- re-entry is a FIXED ~19,800/agent and amortises, so long units are untested and the 27-call dispatch that motivated the lever is exactly that untested regime. Do not overclaim in either direction.

THE MECHANISM, which generalises past this repo: a split does not divide the call count. One agent batched six files into 5 calls; three agents needed 12. Lower context per call (31,836 vs 56,417) did not recover it. The calls^1.54 fit was estimated across agents doing DIFFERENT tasks, so it conflated 'longer agents cost superlinearly more' with 'agents given bigger tasks cost more'; holding the task fixed separates them and the second effect was doing the work.

#26 SCORED PASS and the treatment really ran this time (resume-probe.jsonl: decision=injected, has_reason_key=true, injected_chars=5993). Opening 44,516 vs the 60,000 bound; 449,515 over the first ten calls vs 1,420,000. BUT the VOID run -- same restart, no handoff -- opened at 48,744, the same band. Nothing separates the arms. It scores that the injection is FREE, not that the handoff SAVES. The next prediction to arm is the one that would actually test it: whether the treated session repeats work the handoff already told it.

METHOD NOTE worth keeping: cost the arms by agentId through agents.read_agent_runs, NOT through 'agent-yield agents'. Three concurrent same-type dispatches are exactly the case the ±120s join documents itself as mismatching; the agent id sidesteps it entirely. Script kept at scratchpad/partE/measure.py -- scratchpad is volatile, so re-derive rather than trust it.
Left undone deliberately: #32's actual fix, and re-scoring Part C after it. Both are the next session's first move, in that order.
